source.author: ov
source.text: Fluctibus erigitur caelumque aequare videtur pontus et inductas aspergine tangere nubes; et modo, cum fulvas ex imo vertit harenas, concolor est illis, Stygia modo nigrior unda, sternitur interdum spumisque sonantibus albet.
source.text_original: Fluctibus erigitur caelumque aequare videtur / pontus et inductas aspergine tangere nubes; / et modo, cum fulvas ex imo vertit harenas, / concolor est illis, Stygia modo nigrior unda, / sternitur interdum spumisque sonantibus albet.
source.text_english: The sea is lifted by the waves and seems to equal the sky and to touch the clouds drawn over it with spray; and now, when it overturns the yellow sands from the depths below, it is the same color as them, now the wave is darker than Stygian darkness, and at times it lies white with resounding foam.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Graia novam ferro molem commenta iuventus pergit et ingenti gaudens domat aequora velo, nec mihi libertas imis freta tollere harenis, qualis eram nondum vinclis et carcere clausus.
reuse.text_original: Graia novam ferro molem commenta iuventus / pergit et ingenti gaudens domat aequora velo, / nec mihi libertas imis freta tollere harenis, / qualis eram nondum vinclis et carcere clausus.
reuse.text_english: The Greek youth goes on devising a new mass of iron and, rejoicing, subdues the seas with a great sail, nor is it freedom for me to lift the deep waters from the lowest sands, such as I was before, not yet shut in by chains and prison.
